import pandas as pd

# File paths for all source CSV files
source_files = {
    "mixed": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/training_0.csv",
    "hispanic": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/training_1.csv",
    "other": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/training_2.csv",
    "asian": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/training_3.csv",
    "whites": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/training_4.csv",
    "black": "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/training_5.csv",
}

# Load all source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_mixed = pd.read_csv(source_files["mixed"], index_col=0)
df_hispanic = pd.read_csv(source_files["hispanic"], index_col=0)
df_other = pd.read_csv(source_files["other"], index_col=0)
df_asian = pd.read_csv(source_files["asian"], index_col=0)
df_whites = pd.read_csv(source_files["whites"], index_col=0)
df_black = pd.read_csv(source_files["black"], index_col=0)

# We have 6 source tables, each with schema:
# ['CountyID', 'CountyName', <population_column>, 'Year', 'ID']
# The target table has 6 groups of columns, each group corresponds to one source table,
# with suffixes _x, _y, _x_9, _x_10, etc. for CountyID and CountyName and Year,
# and the population columns renamed accordingly.

# The plan:
# 1. Rename columns in each source table to match the target schema columns for that source.
# 2. Join all source tables on ['CountyID', 'CountyName', 'Year', 'ID'] keys.
#    Since all source tables have these keys, we join on these 4 columns.
# 3. After join, reorder columns to match exactly the target schema order.
# 4. Export the final dataframe to the target CSV path.

# Rename columns in each source dataframe to match target schema columns:

# Source 4 (whites_population) -> suffix _x
df_whites_renamed = df_whites.rename(columns={
    "CountyID": "CountyID_x",
    "CountyName": "CountyName_x",
    "whites_population": "whites_population",
    "Year": "Year_x",
    "ID": "ID"
})

# Source 2 (other_population) -> suffix _y
df_other_renamed = df_other.rename(columns={
    "CountyID": "CountyID_y",
    "CountyName": "CountyName_y",
    "other_population": "other_population",
    "Year": "Year_y",
    "ID": "ID"
})

# Source 0 (mixed_population) -> suffix _x_9 and CountyName_x_10 (two different names for CountyName)
df_mixed_renamed = df_mixed.rename(columns={
    "CountyID": "CountyID_x_9",
    "CountyName": "CountyName_x_10",
    "mixed_population": "mixed_population",
    "Year": "Year_x_12",
    "ID": "ID"
})

# Source 1 (hispanic_population) -> suffix _y_13 and CountyName_y_14
df_hispanic_renamed = df_hispanic.rename(columns={
    "CountyID": "CountyID_y_13",
    "CountyName": "CountyName_y_14",
    "hispanic_population": "hispanic_population",
    "Year": "Year_y_16",
    "ID": "ID"
})

# Source 5 (black_population) -> suffix _x_17 and CountyName_x_18
df_black_renamed = df_black.rename(columns={
    "CountyID": "CountyID_x_17",
    "CountyName": "CountyName_x_18",
    "black_population": "black_population",
    "Year": "Year_x_20",
    "ID": "ID"
})

# Source 3 (asian_population) -> suffix _y_21 and CountyName_y_22
df_asian_renamed = df_asian.rename(columns={
    "CountyID": "CountyID_y_21",
    "CountyName": "CountyName_y_22",
    "asian_population": "asian_population",
    "Year": "Year_y_24",
    "ID": "ID"
})

# Now join all dataframes on the 'ID' column (unique key) to avoid ambiguity and ensure one-to-one join
# Because ID is unique and present in all tables, join on ID is safe and simpler.

# Start with whites_population dataframe as base
df_joined = df_whites_renamed

# Join with other_population
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_other_renamed.drop(columns=["CountyID_y", "CountyName_y", "Year_y"]), on="ID", how="inner")

# Join with mixed_population
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_mixed_renamed.drop(columns=["CountyID_x_9", "CountyName_x_10", "Year_x_12"]), on="ID", how="inner")

# Join with hispanic_population
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_hispanic_renamed.drop(columns=["CountyID_y_13", "CountyName_y_14", "Year_y_16"]), on="ID", how="inner")

# Join with black_population
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_black_renamed.drop(columns=["CountyID_x_17", "CountyName_x_18", "Year_x_20"]), on="ID", how="inner")

# Join with asian_population
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_asian_renamed.drop(columns=["CountyID_y_21", "CountyName_y_22", "Year_y_24"]), on="ID", how="inner")

# After these merges, the dataframe has all population columns and all CountyID_x, CountyName_x, Year_x, etc. columns from whites_population only.
# But we need to add the other CountyID_x/y and CountyName_x/y and Year_x/y columns from other sources as separate columns.

# To get those columns, we merge again but this time to get those columns only (CountyID_x/y, CountyName_x/y, Year_x/y) from each source.

# Extract the key columns from each source for the target columns:

# From whites_population (already in df_joined)
# From other_population
df_other_keys = df_other_renamed[["ID", "CountyID_y", "CountyName_y", "Year_y"]]

# From mixed_population
df_mixed_keys = df_mixed_renamed[["ID", "CountyID_x_9", "CountyName_x_10", "Year_x_12"]]

# From hispanic_population
df_hispanic_keys = df_hispanic_renamed[["ID", "CountyID_y_13", "CountyName_y_14", "Year_y_16"]]

# From black_population
df_black_keys = df_black_renamed[["ID", "CountyID_x_17", "CountyName_x_18", "Year_x_20"]]

# From asian_population
df_asian_keys = df_asian_renamed[["ID", "CountyID_y_21", "CountyName_y_22", "Year_y_24"]]

# Merge these keys into df_joined on ID
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_other_keys, on="ID", how="inner")
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_mixed_keys, on="ID", how="inner")
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_hispanic_keys, on="ID", how="inner")
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_black_keys, on="ID", how="inner")
df_joined = df_joined.merge(df_asian_keys, on="ID", how="inner")

# Now df_joined should have all columns needed.

# Reorder columns to match exactly the target schema order:
target_columns = [
    'CountyID_x', 'CountyName_x', 'whites_population', 'Year_x', 'ID',
    'CountyID_y', 'CountyName_y', 'other_population', 'Year_y',
    'CountyID_x_9', 'CountyName_x_10', 'mixed_population', 'Year_x_12',
    'CountyID_y_13', 'CountyName_y_14', 'hispanic_population', 'Year_y_16',
    'CountyID_x_17', 'CountyName_x_18', 'black_population', 'Year_x_20',
    'CountyID_y_21', 'CountyName_y_22', 'asian_population', 'Year_y_24'
]

# Check if all target columns are present
missing_cols = [col for col in target_columns if col not in df_joined.columns]
if missing_cols:
    raise ValueError(f"Missing columns in the joined dataframe: {missing_cols}")

df_final = df_joined[target_columns]

# Ensure correct dtypes as per target schema:
# According to target schema:
# CountyID_x, CountyID_y, CountyID_x_9, CountyID_y_13, CountyID_x_17, CountyID_y_21: integer
# CountyName_x, CountyName_y, CountyName_x_10, CountyName_y_14, CountyName_x_18, CountyName_y_22: string
# whites_population, other_population, mixed_population, hispanic_population, black_population, asian_population: integer
# Year_x, Year_y, Year_x_12, Year_y_16, Year_x_20, Year_y_24: integer
# ID: integer

int_columns = [
    'CountyID_x', 'whites_population', 'Year_x',
    'ID',
    'CountyID_y', 'other_population', 'Year_y',
    'CountyID_x_9', 'mixed_population', 'Year_x_12',
    'CountyID_y_13', 'hispanic_population', 'Year_y_16',
    'CountyID_x_17', 'black_population', 'Year_x_20',
    'CountyID_y_21', 'asian_population', 'Year_y_24'
]

str_columns = [
    'CountyName_x',
    'CountyName_y',
    'CountyName_x_10',
    'CountyName_y_14',
    'CountyName_x_18',
    'CountyName_y_22'
]

# Convert integer columns
for col in int_columns:
    df_final[col] = pd.to_numeric(df_final[col], errors='raise').astype(int)

# Convert string columns
for col in str_columns:
    df_final[col] = df_final[col].astype(str)

# Write the final dataframe to CSV
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_5/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_final.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
